newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak on higher dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak on higher dlr demand.

text.p: The Philippine peso fell to 26.246 to the dollar at the close of Monday's session from 26.243, weakened by the higher corporate demand for dollars, traders said.
The day's average was at 26.246 versus 26.239 on Friday. Volume thinned to $78.60 million from $134.00 million.
"There was demand from the corporates," said a local bank dealer.
Dealers said the peso should have been stronger due to the higher interest rates in the money market.
Due to the higher demand for dollars, the peso fetched a lower rate in the grey market of 26.275 from 26.255, dealers said, pulling down the peso to a day-low of 26.248 pesos in the official market.
The Central Bank stayed away from the market since the peso traded within its desired range of 26.23 to 26.25.
Dealers said the peso could recover on Tuesday if the high interest rates persisted in the money market.
